meta.title_plain: How to guard your accounts like a pro
meta.teaser: Five steps to strong passwords, spotting scams and keeping your secrets secret.

page.title: How to guard your accounts like a pro
page.sub: A skill you can use today
page.bigIdea: Most hacked accounts aren't cracked by geniuses. They're handed over by tricks, so a few smart habits keep you way ahead.

cards.title: Make it long and random
cards.front: What makes a password hard to crack?
cards.back: Length beats tricks. The UK's cyber experts suggest three random words, like applenemobiro. In 2019, about 23 million hacked accounts used 123456.
cards.tryit: Invent three silly passwords from three random words each. Don't use them, just practise the idea.

cards.title: One account, one password
cards.front: Why not use one great password everywhere?
cards.back: If one site leaks it, crooks try it everywhere. US safety agency CISA tells how Emma got hacked this way. A password manager remembers them all.
cards.tryit: Count how many accounts you have: games, school, email. Ask Dad about a password manager.

cards.title: Turn on 2-step verification
cards.front: What if someone steals your password anyway?
cards.back: 2-step verification asks for a second code, often from an app. Roblox says no one else can log in, even knowing your password. It's like a second lock.
cards.tryit: With Dad, open Roblox Settings, then Security, and check if 2-step verification is on.

cards.title: Spot the bait
cards.front: How can you tell a message is a scam?
cards.back: Watch for rush ('act now!'), weird links, spelling mistakes and prizes. Roblox says every 'free Robux' offer is a scam. Too good to be true usually is.
cards.tryit: Invent a fake 'free Brawl Stars gems' message. Circle three clues that give it away.

cards.title: Guard your secrets
cards.front: What should you never share in games or chats?
cards.back: Never share passwords, login codes, your address or school. Roblox staff will never ask for your password. If something feels off, report it and tell an adult.
cards.tryit: Write a list of five things you'd never type in a game chat. Stick it near your desk.

words.d: A trick message that tries to get your password or details.
A password made of several random words joined together.
A second check, like a code, after you type your password.
An app that makes and safely remembers all your passwords.
When a company's saved information gets stolen by hackers.

quiz.hint: Think about what a stranger could guess from your profile, and which trick hackers already know.
quiz.why: Three random words are long and unpredictable, while names, years and swapped letters are easy to guess.

quiz.q: A message says: 'Click now for 10,000 free Robux! Only 5 minutes left!' What do you do?
opts: Click fast before time runs out
quiz.hint: Two clues here are on the scam checklist. Can you spot them?
quiz.why: Free Robux plus a rush to act are classic scam signs, and Roblox says no free Robux offer is real.

quiz.q: A crook learns your password. What stops them logging in?
quiz.hint: Which step adds a second lock that needs something only you have?
quiz.why: 2-step verification asks for a code from your phone or app, which the crook doesn't have.

quiz.q: A friendly player says they work for Roblox and need your login code. What's true?
opts: Staff sometimes need codes to help
It's fine if they seem nice
Roblox staff never ask for this
quiz.why: Real staff never ask for passwords or codes, so anyone who does is trying to take your account.
